Mr. President, distinguished Council members, dear delegates, the draft resolution before the Human Rights Council under the code A/HR/7/37/L/1 bears the title The human rights situation in the east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It basically requests the following that the High Commissioner for Human Rights urgently establishes a fact-finding mission on the serious violations of human rights and the serious violations of international humanitarian law committed in North and South Kivu provinces in the east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo with a clear mandate, notably to investigate and establish the facts and circumstances and basic roots of all the allegations of human rights violations and attacks on them and violations of international humanitarian law, including those which have targeted women and children and which involve gender based and sexual violence. It must also collect and analyse evidence, particularly in cases against women and children, and that all the documentation and evidence be safely guarded, including the forensic materials, with a view to future judicial proceedings. Through the resolution, the Human Rights Council expects that the High Commissioner for Human Rights will draft recommendations and take on responsibility, which would attach responsibility for bringing an end to impunity and also establish individual accountability. There will be an oral update in the 59th session following an enhanced interactive dialogue. And this will also be followed up at the 60th session with an oral update again and another enhanced interactive dialogue. In order to combat impunity and to prevent a repetition of these violations, attacks on human rights and violations of international humanitarian law, the Council calls on Rwanda to express the respect, the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and withdraw its troops from the territory in order to perpetuate a culture of accountability for human rights violations in that part of the Democratic Republic of the Congo which is regularly subject to attacks and negative forces effects will also call for the establishment of a commission of inquiry which will work in conjunction with the fact finding mission and have the same mandate. So my delegation calls on your solidarity once again, which you showed already towards the Congolese people through your mass support for an adoption by consensus of this resolution. Thank you.

Mr. President, the convening of this special session reflects the Human Rights Council's responsiveness and commitment to addressing urgent crisis. Our approach must be balanced, constructive, and solutions oriented. All parties must be encouraged to engage openly in dialogue as it is essential for resolving the conflict. While accountability remains crucial, it must not come at the cost of undermining opportunities for an inclusive political solutions for the region. Therefore, any emergency fact-finding mission must operate with impartiality, independence, and full transparency. Mr. President, we recognize the complex history behind this crisis, including colonial legacies. Regional solutions led by African nations remain key to achieving lasting peace. We commend regional partners for their efforts to promote peace and stability in the region. We urge all parties to return to peace negotiations and end the cycle of hostilities before more lives are lost. Moreover, Indonesia calls for all parties to ensure immediate humanitarian access, including urgent medical assistance. We also urge international partners to scale up supports, food, medical aid and shelter are desperately needed, especially for women and children. We hope for an end to violence and a path toward lasting peace and prosperity in the region. Finally, Indonesia reaffirms our unwavering respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC and thus supports the adoptions of the draft resolutions by consensus. I thank you.
